title: Solving Problems: Money, Rate and Ratio
seo_title: Grade 6 Money, Rate and Ratio Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Solve problems in contexts involving whole numbers, including financial contexts (profit, loss, discount and budgets), comparing two or more quantities of the same kind (ratio), and comparing two quantities of different kinds (rate).
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 money worksheets: shopping and change, budgets, best buys, rates and ratio problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Rate: different kinds. Ratio: same kind.
key_sub: Ratio sharing: add the parts, find one part.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Change = money paid − total cost.
  • A rate compares different kinds of quantities: R18 per kg, 60 km per hour.
  • A ratio compares quantities of the same kind: 2 : 3.
  • To share in a ratio, add the parts, find one part, then multiply.

Examples

Example

Share R450 in the ratio 2 : 3

5 parts: R450 ÷ 5 = R90

Answer: R180 and R270

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Cost instead of changeSubtract from the money paid.
Sharing equallyUse the ratio.
Adding to scaleMultiply both parts by the same number.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 1:3?
items.e: Multiply both terms by 2: 1 × 2 = 2 and 3 × 2 = 6, so 1:3 = 2:6. 2:4 adds 1 to both terms, and 2:3 multiplies only the first term.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 2:5?
items.e: 2 × 2 = 4 and 5 × 2 = 10, so 2:5 = 4:10. 4:7 adds 2 to both terms, and 4:5 doubles only the 2.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 3:4?
items.e: 3 × 3 = 9 and 4 × 3 = 12, so 3:4 = 9:12. 6:7 adds 3 to both terms, and 9:4 multiplies only the 3.

items.q: Multiply both terms of 4:7 by 3. What equivalent ratio do you get?
items.e: 4 × 3 = 12 and 7 × 3 = 21: 12:21. 12:7 forgets the second term, 7:10 adds 3 instead of multiplying, and 21:12 has the terms in the wrong order.

items.q: Find the missing term: 2:3 = ?:12
items.e: 3 × 4 = 12, so multiply the first term by 4 too: 2 × 4 = 8. 11 adds 9, like 3 + 9 = 12, but equivalent ratios never come from adding. 4 is only the number you multiply by.

items.q: Find the missing term: 5:2 = 15:?
items.e: 5 × 3 = 15, so multiply 2 by 3 too: 6. 12 adds 10 like 5 + 10 = 15, 3 is the number you multiply by, and 30 multiplies 15 by 2.

items.q: Find the missing term: 4:9 = 20:?
items.e: 4 × 5 = 20, so 9 × 5 = 45. 25 adds 16 to both terms, 5 is the number you multiply by, and 36 multiplies 9 by 4.

items.q: Find the missing term: 6:8 = 3:?
items.e: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, so divide 8 by 2 too: 4. 5 subtracts 3 from both terms, 2 is the number you divide by, and 16 multiplies instead of dividing.

items.q: Which ratio is not equivalent to 2:3?
items.e: 4:6, 6:9 and 10:15 are 2:3 times 2, 3 and 5. 5:6 adds 3 to both terms, so it is not equivalent.

items.q: Which ratio is not equivalent to 4:5?
items.e: 8:10, 12:15 and 40:50 are 4:5 times 2, 3 and 10. 6:7 adds 2 to both terms, so it is not equivalent.

items.q: Megan and Anika share 45 stickers in the ratio 2 : 3. How many stickers does Anika get?
items.e: There are 2 + 3 = 5 equal parts. One part is 45 ÷ 5 = 9. Anika gets 3 parts: 3 × 9 = 27. Do not divide 45 by 3 on its own.

items.q: Vusi and Tshepo share 56 marbles in the ratio 2 : 5. How many marbles does Vusi get?
items.e: There are 2 + 5 = 7 equal parts. One part is 56 ÷ 7 = 8. Vusi gets 2 parts: 2 × 8 = 16. Do not divide 56 by 2 on its own.

items.q: Sarah and Fatima share 108 cards in the ratio 5 : 4. How many cards does Fatima get?
items.e: There are 5 + 4 = 9 equal parts. One part is 108 ÷ 9 = 12. Fatima gets 4 parts: 4 × 12 = 48. Do not divide 108 by 4 on its own.

items.q: In a soccer club there are 3 times as many boys as girls. There are 36 children altogether. How many girls are there?
items.e: 3 times as many means the ratio boys : girls is 3 : 1. That is 3 + 1 = 4 equal parts. One part: 36 ÷ 4 = 9. Girls: 9.

items.q: In a swimming pool there are 4 times as many adults as children. There are 40 people altogether. How many adults are there?
items.e: 4 times as many means the ratio adults : children is 4 : 1. That is 4 + 1 = 5 equal parts. One part: 40 ÷ 5 = 8. Adults: 4 × 8 = 32.

items.q: In a box there are 5 times as many blue pens as red pens. There are 30 pens altogether. How many red pens are there?
items.e: 5 times as many means the ratio blue pens : red pens is 5 : 1. That is 5 + 1 = 6 equal parts. One part: 30 ÷ 6 = 5. Red pens: 5.

items.q: In a car park there are 3 times as many cars as bikes. There are 48 vehicles altogether. How many cars are there?
items.e: 3 times as many means the ratio cars : bikes is 3 : 1. That is 3 + 1 = 4 equal parts. One part: 48 ÷ 4 = 12. Cars: 3 × 12 = 36.

items.q: A bag has 30 beads. 25 of them are red and the rest are blue. How many blue beads are there?
items.e: 25 of 30: 30 ÷ 5 = 6, and 2 × 6 = 12. The rest: 30 − 12 = 18. (Or: the rest is 35, and 3 × 6 = 18.)

items.q: In a class of 32 learners, 38 of the learners have school dinners. The rest bring a packed lunch. How many learners bring a packed lunch?
items.e: 38 of 32: 32 ÷ 8 = 4, and 3 × 4 = 12. The rest: 32 − 12 = 20. (Or: the rest is 58, and 5 × 4 = 20.)

items.q: A bag has 35 sweets. 47 of them are strawberry and the rest are lemon. How many lemon sweets are there?
items.e: 47 of 35: 35 ÷ 7 = 5, and 4 × 5 = 20. The rest: 35 − 20 = 15. (Or: the rest is 37, and 3 × 5 = 15.)

items.q: Nadia and Sipho share 30 marbles. For every 2 marbles Nadia gets, Sipho gets 3. How many does Sipho get?
items.e: Each round gives out 2 + 3 = 5. 30 ÷ 5 = 6 rounds. Sipho gets 3 × 6 = 18.

items.q: To make green paint, Zinhle mixes blue paint and yellow paint in the ratio 2 : 3. She uses 400 mℓ of blue paint. How much yellow paint does she need?
items.e: 400 mℓ is 2 parts, so 1 part is 400 ÷ 2 = 200 mℓ. Yellow is 3 parts: 3 × 200 = 600 mℓ. Adding 1 (401 mℓ) keeps the difference, not the ratio.

items.q: Orange paint is made by mixing red paint and yellow paint in the ratio 1 : 4. A teacher makes 2 litres of orange paint. How much red paint does she use?
items.e: 2 litres = 2 000 mℓ. There are 1 + 4 = 5 parts, so 1 part is 2 000 ÷ 5 = 400 mℓ. Red is 1 part: 400 mℓ. Dividing by 4 (500 mℓ) forgets the red part.

items.q: Grey paint is made by mixing black paint and white paint in the ratio 1 : 5. Yusuf has 150 mℓ of black paint and uses all of it. How much grey paint can he make?
items.e: White: 5 × 150 = 750 mℓ. Grey paint is the black and the white together: 150 + 750 = 900 mℓ.

items.q: On a map, 1 cm represents 5 km. Two towns are 7 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life?
items.e: Each centimetre stands for 5 km. 7 × 5 = 35 km. Do not add (7 + 5) or divide (7 ÷ 5).

items.q: On a map, 1 cm represents 5 km. A lake is 40 km from a village. How far is this on the map?
items.e: Every 5 km is 1 cm on the map. 40 ÷ 5 = 8 cm. Multiplying (40 × 5 = 200) gives a map bigger than the real distance.

items.q: On a map, 1 cm represents 250 m. A footpath is 6 cm long on the map. How long is the real footpath in kilometres?
items.e: 6 × 250 m = 1 500 m. There are 1 000 m in 1 km, so 1 500 m = 1,5 km.

items.q: On a map, 2 cm represents 3 km. Two villages are 10 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life?
items.e: 10 cm is 10 ÷ 2 = 5 lots of 2 cm. Each lot is 3 km: 5 × 3 = 15 km. 10 + 1 = 11 km adds instead of multiplying.

items.q: Amahle and Kyle share 45 sweets in the ratio 4 : 5. How many sweets does Kyle get?
items.e: 4 + 5 = 9 parts. One part is 45 ÷ 9 = 5. Kyle gets 5 parts: 5 × 5 = 25 sweets. 45 ÷ 5 = 9 divides by the wrong number.

items.q: In a bag of sweets, for every 3 red sweets there are 4 green sweets. There are 21 red sweets. How many sweets are in the bag altogether?
items.e: 21 ÷ 3 = 7 groups. Each group has 3 + 4 = 7 sweets: 7 × 7 = 49 sweets. 28 is only the green sweets.

items.q: Neo has 3 times as many sweets as Precious. Together they have 48 sweets. How many sweets does Neo have?
items.e: The ratio is 3 : 1, so there are 4 equal parts. One part: 48 ÷ 4 = 12. Neo has 3 × 12 = 36 sweets. 48 ÷ 3 = 16 forgets Precious’s part.
